info.name: Gen UI API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Gen UI backend.

## Getting going

1. Start the stack: `docker compose up --build`.
2. Run **Auth > Sign in**. It stores `accessToken` for you, and the collection sends it as a bearer token on everything else.
3. Anything else. When a request starts answering 401, run **Auth > Rotate the session**.

Step 2 is a convenience rather than a requirement: a collection-level pre-request script signs in for you whenever there is no token, so any request runs on its own and **Run collection** stays green even though **Sign out** clears the token partway through.

## Variables

`baseUrl` points at the API through nginx (`http://localhost:5173/api`), the same origin the browser uses. Running the API with `pnpm dev` instead? Set it to `http://localhost:3000/api`.

`email` and `password` are the credentials **Sign in** uses. All five seeded accounts share the password `Password123!`; `admin@example.com` is the one that may reach `/users`.

## A note on the Origin check

`/auth/*` rejects a browser `Origin` that is neither the API's own host nor an allowed CORS origin. Postman sends no `Origin`, which the guard treats as a non-browser caller and allows. If you add one by hand, it has to match `baseUrl`.

## Keeping this in sync

This file is maintained by hand. The generated alternative is always current: import `http://localhost:5173/docs/openapi.json` into Postman, or read it at `http://localhost:5173/docs`.

exec: // Signs in on demand, so every request works on its own and a full
// collection run stays green after Sign out has cleared the token.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Sign in first: **Sign in** writes `accessToken` into the collection variables, and every other request picks it up from there.

The refresh token never appears in a body - it is an httpOnly cookie scoped to `/api/auth`. Postman's cookie jar keeps it, so **Rotate the session** and **Sign out** work with no extra setup.

request.description:
Exchanges credentials for a 15-minute access token, and sets the refresh cookie.

Change `email` / `password` in the collection variables to sign in as someone else. Every seeded account uses `Password123!`.
The account behind the current access token. A 401 here means the token expired - run **Rotate the session**.

No body: the refresh cookie is the credential. Every call replaces both the cookie and the access token.

Replaying a spent token outside a 10-second grace window revokes the whole login - so if this starts answering 401 with `code: REFRESH_REUSED`, sign in again.
Revokes the presented token family and clears the cookie. Answers 204 even without a cookie, so it is safe to call twice.

item.name: Profile
item.description: The signed-in user's own account - available to every role, unlike `/users`.

request.description: The same payload as `/auth/me`.
Display name only. The schema is strict: sending `email`, `role` or `isActive` is a 400, not a silent no-op. Try it - that 400 is the privilege boundary being visible.

**This really changes the password** of whichever account is signed in, and re-seeding will not put it back (the seed skips rows that already exist).

Every other session for the account is revoked in the same transaction; the response carries a replacement token pair, so this client stays signed in. The test below also moves `newPassword` into `password` so the rest of the collection keeps working.

exec: // The old password is gone; keep the collection runnable.

item.name: Users (admin)
item.description: The user directory. Every route here is ADMIN-only - signing in as `liam.carter@example.com` and retrying is the quickest way to see the 403.

request.description: `search` matches email or name anywhere in the value, case-insensitively. `status` is `ACTIVE` or `DEACTIVATED`. `lastSignIn` is `never` (no sign-in yet) or a date such as `2026-05-03` (last sign-in on that day in `timeZone`, default UTC). The optional filters are switched off below - tick them in the Params tab.

The only way an account comes into existence - there is no public sign-up.

The pre-request script stamps the email with a timestamp so this stays re-runnable; without that, the second run is a 409.

exec: // A fresh address each run, so re-running never hits the unique-email 409.

request.description: Uses the id saved by **Create a user**. Any UUID works; a non-UUID is a 400 and an unknown one a 404.

Send only the fields to change. Demoting or deactivating an account also revokes its refresh tokens, in the same transaction, so its sessions end at once.

Two rules the API enforces: an admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves (403), and the last active admin cannot be demoted (409).
Id and name of every active account. Open to every role — the one users route that is not admin-only.

item.name: Assets
item.description: The asset tree: regions, sites, areas, equipment. Every list endpoint in the app takes the same kind of query — `page`/`pageSize`, `sort=field` or `sort=-field`, comma-separated multi-value filters, `range` (relative) or `from`/`to`, and `search`. The web app uses exactly these params in its URLs.

item.name: Assistant
item.description: **Asking spends provider tokens on every call.** Needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; without it the chat answers 503. Conversations are saved per user: the requests below share one conversation id.

request.description:
Replies as an AI SDK UI message stream over SSE, so Postman shows `data:` frames arriving rather than one JSON body. Some frames are tool calls that the web app renders as React components (set `generateUi` to false for a Markdown-only answer).

The server keeps the conversation: send only the new `message` (its id is a fresh `{{$guid}}` on every send) and keep `id` the same across turns. `"trigger": "regenerate-message"` without a message answers the last question again.

`model` is one of `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5` or `claude-haiku-4-5` (the default and cheapest, used here). Add `"effort": "low"` … `"max"` for Opus and Sonnet; Haiku ignores it.

`timeZone` (IANA, default `UTC`) is where "today" and the dates in the question are read. Ask in English or Serbian; other languages get a short refusal.
Your most recent conversation, every message with its parts, as the web app restores it. `conversation` is null when there is none. Free: no model call.

For the roles of the form's tool: admins, except the logbook forms, which everyone has. When the assistant opens a form in an answer (`createUser`, `createAlarmRule`, `editAlarmRule`, `createDevice`, `editDevice`, `createTag`, `editTag`, `createAsset`, `editAsset`, `createLogbookEntry`, `editLogbookEntry`), the tool call ends there; the user saves through the page's own endpoint (`POST /users`, or `POST` or `PATCH` on `/alarm-definitions`, `/devices`, `/tags`, `/assets` or `/logbook`). The web app then calls this with `saved` and the saved record's id, or with `{ "status": "closed" }` when the form was closed unsaved. The server reads the record and adds `outcome` to that tool call's output in the saved conversation, so a reload shows the result and Claude knows on its next turn. Returns the output with its outcome.

Replace the last path segment with a form call's `toolCallId` from "Saved conversation" (a part of type `tool-<form tool name>`, e.g. `tool-createUser` or `tool-editDevice`). For an edit form, `entityId` must be the record the form edits. Once per form: a second call is a 409. Free: no model call.
Deletes the conversation used by "Ask the assistant" for good. 204 even when there was nothing to delete.

item.name: Health
item.description: Both are public - no token needed.

request.description: No dependencies: answers as long as the process can serve. This is what the Docker healthcheck calls, so a database blip never restarts a healthy container.
Pings the database and answers 503 when it is unreachable. Use it for load-balancer membership, not for restarts.
